teaser.text: First Quantum Minerals is a Canadian mining company that turns rock into copper products, with smaller businesses in nickel, gold and other recovered materials. Its dollar comes in when customers pay for saleable metal and goes out through mining, processing, delivery, upkeep, financing, taxes and growth.

stock.opening: The weighted scenario is CAD 24.87 in October 2027, CAD 29.61 in October 2028 and CAD 39.32 in October 2029. It hinges on operating recovery, debt reduction and Panama’s legal path.
stock.closing: The full memo also covers First Quantum’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could First Quantum's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast points to downside over one and two years, followed by a small positive return by October 2029. The probability-weighted price is CAD 24.87 in October 2027, CAD 29.61 in October 2028 and CAD 39.32 in October 2029, including dividends. Against today’s CAD 37.87, those returns are negative 34%, negative 22% and positive 4%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for First Quantum?

paragraphs.text: EBITDA is the central operating driver. The base case holds it near USD 2.5 billion across the forecast, at USD 2.543 billion, USD 2.586 billion and USD 2.534 billion. It uses midpoint copper guidance, S3 and Enterprise production, and no full Panama restart. Management guides to copper production of 410–470 thousand tonnes in 2027 and 430–490 thousand tonnes in 2028.

The bear case falls from USD 734 million to USD 210 million because copper output and margins weaken, Zambia remains costly and Panama contributes no restart production. The bull case rises from USD 3.598 billion to USD 5.215 billion because costs improve, copper prices are stronger and a partial Panama restart adds production in the final year. First Quantum’s history supports caution: adjusted EBITDA declined sharply before its modest 2025 recovery.

blocks.heading: How much cash does First Quantum really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow therefore needs a stricter reading. After capital spending, lease payments and interest, cash can be negative even when operating cash is positive. Receivables make the problem sharper: Zambian VAT remained tied up rather than available for debt service. The cash-flow table shows what survives after the main cash claims.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for First Quantum today?

paragraphs.text: The price-to-earnings ratio, or P/E, compares the share price with earnings per share. A forward P/E uses expected earnings, so it can look reasonable while the latest quarter reported US$136 million of attributable earnings alongside an adjusted loss of US$106 million. The adjustment may remove unusual items, but it remains management’s definition, and accounting earnings are not cash.

blocks.heading: What has First Quantum guided for 2026?

paragraphs.text: Management’s plan is to raise copper output while bringing costs down, but it needs a strong second half and relief from Zambia’s power problem. Guidance is a plan, not a guarantee. Growth is shifting toward Kansanshi as the S3 expansion adds processing capacity, while Cobre Panamá contributes temporary copper from stockpiles.

blocks.heading: Did First Quantum keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Promises about projects can be tested more directly. In January 2025, management forecast first production from Kansanshi’s S3 expansion in the second half of that year. First production means initial usable output; commercial production means the operation has moved beyond testing and ramp-up into reliable normal work. First concentrate arrived in August, and commercial production followed on December 1. The project therefore met a concrete delivery milestone, even as Sentinel’s production fell because of lower grades and greater maintenance.

blocks.heading: What has First Quantum’s recent revenue and profit trend been?

paragraphs.text: Revenue reached its high point in 2022, fell through the next two years and recovered in 2025. Copper sales rose in 2025, while the realized copper price rose faster. That combination explains much of the revenue improvement, but it describes price and shipment value rather than a comparable expansion of mining capacity.

Gross margin stayed broadly stable in 2025, and operating income improved. Yet the company still reported a small net loss. Operating income measures the mines and business before financing and taxes; net income is what remains after those claims. A profitable restaurant can still lose money after rent, loan interest and tax.

blocks.heading: What should people watch in First Quantum’s next results?

paragraphs.text: The next results will show whether better production becomes spendable cash. First Quantum is scheduled to report third-quarter results on October 28, 2026, with its call the following day. Investors should compare Kansanshi and Sentinel with their annual targets, then follow unit costs and operating cash.
